issues.description: The problem statement requires Farm to use a List and specifically instructs to initialize an ArrayList in the no-arg constructor, but the provided solution implements the farm collection as a Queue backed by a LinkedList (and its getter/setter use Queue<Animal>). This type mismatch between the specified collection type (List/ArrayList) and the solution (Queue/LinkedList) is a structural inconsistency that can confuse students about which collection type to use and may cause tests or student implementations that follow the specification (List/ArrayList) to diverge from the reference solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the collection type across artifacts. Either update the solution to use a List<Animal> (e.g., private List<Animal> animals = new ArrayList<>(); and adjust imports and getter/setter signatures to List<Animal>) to match the problem statement, or revise the problem statement to accept and describe a Queue/LinkedList implementation. Preferably change the solution to use List/ArrayList so it matches the explicit instruction in the problem description.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML explicitly specify the Farm's animals attribute as a List<Animal> to be implemented using an ArrayList, but the provided solution declares the attribute as Queue<Animal> and initializes it with a LinkedList. This type mismatch (List/ArrayList vs Queue/LinkedList) departs from the stated requirement and can confuse students when mapping the problem instructions (which name List/ArrayList) to the solution/template implementation (which uses Queue/LinkedList).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent with the problem statement: declare the field as List<Animal> animals and initialize it as a new ArrayList<>() in the no-arg constructor (import java.util.List and java.util.ArrayList). Update the getter/setter signatures to use List<Animal> as well. Alternatively, if Queue/LinkedList is intentional, update the problem statement/UML to specify Queue/LinkedList to avoid confusion.
